- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 3–5% relative to model output.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates downside risk; add 2–4% buffer to forecast lows.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% above recent mean), model frequently overcorrects and overshoots; cap forecast peak at 10% above prior high.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish within 5 days, model often fails to adjust; apply mean reversion to forecast 3–5 days ahead, aligning with 14-day moving average.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overestimate volatility in early horizon (days 1–7); reduce forecast by 1–2% per day for days 1–7 if sentiment is neutral or bearish.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.67” or “1.00” patterns, model exhibits persistent bias; apply sentiment-weighted correction: +0.5% for bullish, -0.5% for bearish, averaged over last 5 sentiment values.
